mainTopic: The three lessons of ״לֹא תְחׇנֵּם״ (no land, no praise, no free gifts), the מחלוקת about free gifts, and the limits on praising and gazing at a gentile woman.
overview: The גמרא gives the source for not letting idolaters get a hold on land in ארץ ישראל: the פסוק ״לֹא תְחׇנֵּם״. Because of its unusual spelling, the פסוק teaches three things: no foothold in the land, no praise (חֵן), and no free gifts (מַתְּנַת חִנָּם). A ברייתא confirms all three readings. The גמרא then shows that the free-gift rule is a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about giving or selling a נבלה to a גר or a גוי, and both sides read the word ״אוֹ״ in their own way. Next it returns to the ban on praise and links it to רב, who forbids saying "How beautiful is this גויה." Stories about רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי עקיבא challenge רב. The גמרא answers that the words were thanks to ה׳, not praise of the woman. Finally, the גמרא asks how looking at her was allowed at all, and begins a ברייתא against gazing at women that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The source: do not give them a resting place in the land
steps.stepSummary: The rule comes from the פסוק ״לֹא תְחָנֵּם״, which is read as 'do not give them חֲנָיָיה in the land.'
steps.simpleTranslation: For the פסוק says, ״לֹא תְחׇנֵּם״. This means: do not give them a resting place (a foothold) in the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source in the תורה for the rule about not letting idolaters get a hold on land. It reads the word תְחָנֵּם as if it came from חֲנָיָיה, meaning camping or settling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning of ״לֹא תְחָנֵּם״ is 'do not show them mercy.' The גמרא reads the letters ח-נ as tied to the word חֲנָיָה, settling down. So the פסוק becomes a ban on giving them a permanent place on the land of ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do not show them mercy' (דברים ז:ב); read here in several ways

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the תורה source behind the practical rule against selling land in ארץ ישראל to idolaters.

phrases.english: For the verse says: "You shall not show them mercy (lo techonem)"
Do not give them a resting place in the land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question about the source for not giving idolaters land.
steps.raayaObject: The rule against giving idolaters a hold on land in ארץ ישראל
steps.raayaSupportSource: ״לֹא תְחָנֵּם״ read as לֹא תִּתֵּן לָהֶם חֲנָיָיה

steps.title: Isn't the verse needed to forbid giving them praise?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that ״לֹא תְחָנֵּם״ is already used for a different lesson: do not give them חֵן (praise or charm).
steps.simpleTranslation: But this ״לֹא תְחׇנֵּם״ is needed for something else. The Merciful One is saying: do not give them חֵן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source from step 1. It says the פסוק is already taken for a different lesson, so it cannot teach the land rule too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תְחָנֵּם can also be read from חֵן, grace or favor. That reading teaches that we should not praise idolaters. If the פסוק is busy teaching this, it seems it cannot also teach about land.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One', meaning ה׳ in the תורה

phrases.english: This "lo techonem" is needed
because this is what the Merciful One is saying:
Do not give them favor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using ״לֹא תְחָנֵּם״ as the source for the land rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is already used for the lesson of not giving חֵן, so it seems unavailable for the land lesson.

steps.title: The spelling teaches both lessons
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק meant only חֵן, it would be spelled תְחוּנֵּם with a ו. The missing ו shows that it teaches two things.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the פסוק should have said ״לֹא תְחוּנֵּם״. Why does it say ״לֹא תְחׇנֵּם״? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by looking at how the word is spelled. Because the spelling is unusual, the פסוק teaches both the חֵן lesson and the land lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A spelling with a ו (תְחוּנֵּם) would point clearly to the root of חֵן. The תורה left out the ו, so the word also connects to חֲנָיָה. The פסוק therefore carries two meanings at once.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the פסוק say (it should have said)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not drop the חֵן reading. It keeps it and adds the land reading on top of it.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say "lo techunem"
phrases.notes: With a ו, the word would clearly come from חֵן.

phrases.english: Why does it say "lo techonem"?
Learn two things from it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Spelling-based: the missing ו allows two readings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק can only teach the חֵן lesson.
steps.terutzMaskana: The missing ו shows that the פסוק teaches both חֵן and חֲנָיָה.

steps.title: Isn't the verse also needed to forbid free gifts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects again: ״לֹא תְחָנֵּם״ is needed for a third lesson, not giving them a מַתְּנַת חִנָּם (a free gift).
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is still needed for this: the Merciful One says, do not give them a free gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second challenge. It points to yet another lesson that seems to take up the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תְחָנֵּם can also be read from חִנָּם, meaning for free. That reading teaches that we should not give idolaters undeserved gifts. Now the פסוק seems stretched across three lessons.

phrases.english: But it is still needed
because this is what the Merciful One said:
Do not give them a free gift!
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. The meaning is the same either way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges again after the answer in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ״לֹא תְחָנֵּם״ can teach the land rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is also used for the lesson about free gifts, so it seems unavailable for the land lesson.

steps.title: The spelling teaches all three lessons
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק meant only חִנָּם, it would say תְחִינֵּם with a י. The spelling without a י shows that it teaches all three lessons.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the פסוק should have said ״לֹא תְחִינֵּם״. Why does it say ״לֹא תְחׇנֵּם״? Learn all of them from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in the same way as before. Because the י is also missing, the פסוק teaches all three lessons together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A spelling with a י (תְחִינֵּם) would point only to חִנָּם. The bare spelling, with neither ו nor י, fits every reading. So it teaches no foothold in the land, no praise, and no free gifts.

keyTerms.meaning: The spelling with a י that would point only to חִנָּם

steps.whatToRemember: The plain spelling of ״לֹא תְחָנֵּם״, with no ו and no י, lets it teach three things: no חֲנָיָה in the land, no חֵן, and no מַתְּנַת חִנָּם.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say "lo techinem"
Why does it say "lo techonem"?
Learn all of them from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן לֵימָא קְרָא לֹא תְחִינֵּם
steps.terutzResolutionType: Spelling-based: the missing י allows a third reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק can only teach the lesson about free gifts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plain spelling teaches all three lessons.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms all three readings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the same three meanings of ״לֹא תְחָנֵּם״: no resting place in the land, no favor, and no free gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches the same: ״לֹא תְחׇנֵּם״ means do not give them a resting place in the land. Another explanation: do not give them favor. Another explanation: do not give them a free gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports its conclusion. The ברייתא reads the פסוק in all three ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא worked out the three readings by its own reasoning. Now it shows that an earlier source already taught exactly the same three lessons. The phrase דָּבָר אַחֵר here adds readings that hold together, not readings that cancel each other out.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא confirms that all three lessons come from ״לֹא תְחָנֵּם״.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא תְחׇנֵּם״ — לֹא תִּתֵּן לָהֶם חֲנָיָיה בַּקַּרְקַע,
phrases.english: "Lo techonem": do not give them a resting place in the land.

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״לֹא תְחׇנֵּם״ — לֹא תִּתֵּן לָהֶם חֵן,
phrases.english: Another explanation: "lo techonem": do not give them favor.

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״לֹא תְחׇנֵּם״ — לֹא תִּתֵּן לָהֶם מַתְּנַת חִנָּם.
phrases.english: Another explanation: "lo techonem": do not give them a free gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the conclusion of step 5 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That ״לֹא תְחָנֵּם״ teaches all three lessons
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that lists all three readings

steps.title: The free-gift rule is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the free-gift rule is itself a מחלוקת תנאים. It begins a ברייתא on the פסוק of נבלה, which shows that a נבלה may also be sold to a גר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The free gift itself is a dispute of תנאים. As a ברייתא teaches: "Do not eat any נבלה; give it to the stranger in your gates so he may eat it, or sell it to a foreigner." From this I would only know giving to a גר and selling to a גוי. How do we know selling to a גר? The פסוק says: "give it... or sell it."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that the rule against giving a free gift to a גוי is not agreed on by everyone. It starts quoting a ברייתא to prove this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 4-5 learned from ״לֹא תְחָנֵּם״ that one may not give a גוי a free gift. Now the גמרא says this lesson is really one side of a מחלוקת. The ברייתא's first point is simple: the word ״אוֹ״ (or) lets you sell the נבלה to a גר too, not only give it to him.

keyTerms.meaning: A free gift, given for nothing in return
It is a dispute between תנאים
An animal that died without proper שחיטה; a Jew may not eat it
Here, a גר תושב: a non-Jew who lives in ארץ ישראל and keeps the seven מצוות of בני נח

phrases.english: And the free gift itself is a dispute of תנאים,
as it is taught in a ברייתא: "You shall not eat any carcass;
to the stranger who is within your gates
phrases.notes: This is the גר תושב, a non-Jew living among us. It is not a convert.

phrases.english: you shall give it, and he shall eat it, or sell it to a foreigner."
I would only know giving it to a גר
and selling it to a גוי.
How do we know selling it to a גר?
The פסוק says: "give it... or sell it."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַתְּנַת חִנָּם גּוּפַהּ תַּנָּאֵי הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After listing the three lessons of ״לֹא תְחָנֵּם״, the גמרא now notes that the third lesson (no free gift) is disputed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on giving a גוי a free gift is a מחלוקת תנאים. The ברייתא first learns that a נבלה may also be sold to a גר.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: both giving and selling to both people
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns that a נבלה may also be given to a גוי. רבי מאיר concludes that both a גר and a גוי may receive it by gift or by sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know giving to a גוי? The פסוק says: "give it, and he shall eat it, or sell it to a foreigner." So you can say that both a גר and a גוי may get it, whether by giving or by selling. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes רבי מאיר's reading: every combination is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reads ״אוֹ״ as "either way works" for both people. So giving a נבלה to a גוי for free is allowed. This means רבי מאיר does not hold the free-gift ban that steps 4-5 learned.

keyTerms.meaning: It turns out you can say (a summing-up phrase)
Both this one and that one

phrases.english: How do we know giving it to a גוי?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״תִּתְּנֶנָּה וַאֲכָלָהּ אוֹ מָכֹר לְנׇכְרִי״,
phrases.english: The פסוק says: "give it, and he shall eat it, or sell it to a foreigner."

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא אַתָּה אוֹמֵר: אֶחָד גֵּר וְאֶחָד גּוֹי
phrases.english: So you can say: both a גר and a גוי,
whether by giving or by selling.
These are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the other combination and gives רבי מאיר's full conclusion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: a נבלה may be given or sold to both a גר and a גוי.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: read the words exactly as written
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the פסוק means exactly what it says: give to a גר, sell to a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the words are as they are written. To a גר by giving, and to a גוי by selling.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the other side of the מחלוקת. רבי יהודה does not stretch the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, a גוי may only buy the נבלה and may not get it as a gift. This fits the free-gift ban from ״לֹא תְחָנֵּם״. That is why the גמרא called the free-gift rule a מחלוקת תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: The words are meant exactly as written

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: anyone, either way. רבי יהודה: גר gets it as a gift, גוי only by sale. The free-gift ban fits רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: the words are as they are written:
to a גר by giving, and to a גוי by selling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי מאיר in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: a נבלה is given only to a גר and sold only to a גוי. So no free gift to a גוי.

steps.title: רבי יהודה explains the word ״אוֹ״
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר's reading looks convincing. רבי יהודה answers that if both options were meant for both people, the פסוק would say "and". The word ״אוֹ״ shows that each option belongs to its own person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר speaks well. But רבי יהודה would tell you: if you think it is as רבי מאיר says, the תורה should have written "give it, and he shall eat it, and sell it." Why do I need "or"? Learn from this that it comes to teach that the words are as written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first admits that רבי מאיר's reading sounds right. Then it explains how רבי יהודה defends his own view from the same word ״אוֹ״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the word ״אוֹ״. רבי מאיר reads it as "either one is fine." רבי יהודה says that if everything were allowed, "and" would be enough. So the ״אוֹ״ must separate the two: giving goes with the גר, selling goes with the גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: He speaks well; his point is good
If it enters your mind (if you think so)
Let the תורה (the Merciful One) write

phrases.english: רבי מאיר is speaking well,
and רבי יהודה would tell you:

phrases.aramaic: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ כִּדְקָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: if you think it is as רבי מאיר says,
let the Torah write: "give it, and he shall eat it, and sell it."
Why do I need "or"?

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ לִדְבָרִים כִּכְתָבָן הוּא דַּאֲתָא.
phrases.english: Learn from it that it comes to teach that the words are as written.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁפִּיר קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אָמַר לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts the two readings side by side and defends רבי יהודה from the wording of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Wording proof: an extra word (״אוֹ״ instead of "and") must teach something
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״אוֹ״ seems to mean you may choose either option for anyone, as רבי מאיר says.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה, ״אוֹ״ separates the options: giving for the גר, selling for the גוי.

steps.title: How רבי מאיר uses ״אוֹ״: the גר comes first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי מאיר does with ״אוֹ״. The answer: it teaches that giving to a גר comes before selling to a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר? That word comes to put giving to a גר ahead of selling to a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי מאיר explains the word ״אוֹ״ after רבי יהודה's point, and then answers for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר agrees that ״אוֹ״ teaches something. But for him it teaches an order of priority, not a limit. If you have a choice, first give it to the גר before selling it to a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: To put first; to give priority

phrases.english: And רבי מאיר?
phrases.notes: He means: what does רבי מאיר do with the word ״אוֹ״?

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא לְאַקְדּוֹמֵי נְתִינָה דְּגֵר לִמְכִירָה דְּגוֹי.
phrases.english: That word is to put giving to a גר ahead of selling to a גוי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי יהודה's ״אוֹ״ argument on behalf of רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra word a different job
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ״אוֹ״ seems to have no purpose in רבי מאיר's view.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״אוֹ״ teaches priority: the גר before the גוי.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: priority needs no פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the גר obviously comes first, because we are commanded to keep him alive. So ״אוֹ״ is free to teach his reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? Since you are commanded to keep a גר alive, and you are not commanded to keep a גוי alive, there is no need for a פסוק to say who comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה does not accept רבי מאיר's use of ״אוֹ״. This closes the back-and-forth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a מצוה to help a גר תושב live, but no such מצוה for a גוי. So it is obvious that the גר comes first, and the Torah would not need ״אוֹ״ to teach it. That leaves ״אוֹ״ for רבי יהודה's lesson: "the words are as written."

keyTerms.meaning: Commanded to keep him alive (to support him)

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides use ״אוֹ״. רבי יהודה: it limits gifts to the גר, so no free gifts to a גוי. רבי מאיר: it only puts the גר first, so a gift to a גוי is allowed. The ״לֹא תְחָנֵּם״ ban on free gifts follows רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: And רבי יהודה would say:
since a גר, you are commanded to keep alive,
and a גוי, you are not commanded to keep alive,
no פסוק is needed to put the גר first.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: כֵּיוָן דְּגֵר אַתָּה מְצוֶּּוה לְהַחְיוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי מאיר's use of ״אוֹ״ from רבי יהודה's side, so his own reading stands.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logic: the lesson is already obvious, so the word must teach something else
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe ״אוֹ״ is needed to teach that the גר comes first.
steps.terutzMaskana: Putting the גר first is obvious from the מצוה to keep him alive, so ״אוֹ״ teaches that the words are as written.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The free-gift ban follows רבי יהודה. רבי מאיר allows a free gift to a גוי.

steps.title: A second reading: do not give them praise
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads ״לֹא תְחׇנֵּם״ as "do not give them חֵן," meaning do not praise גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: "Do not show them favor" means: do not give them charm, do not speak of them with praise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא from step 6 and quotes its second reading: a ban on praising גוים. This sets up the next step, where the reading is linked to רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תְחׇנֵּם sounds like חֵן, charm or grace. So this reading forbids giving גוים charm with your words, for example by praising them. The גמרא already analyzed the third reading (free gifts) and now turns to this second reading of the same ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Another explanation of the same פסוק

phrases.english: Another explanation: "Do not show them favor"
means: do not give them charm.
phrases.notes: The word תְחׇנֵּם sounds like חֵן, so the ברייתא reads it as a ban on praising them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״לֹא תְחׇנֵּם״ — לֹא תִּתֵּן לָהֶם חֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the side discussion about free gifts, the גמרא returns to the second clause of the ברייתא from step 6 (no חֵן) in order to analyze it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is forbidden to give גוים חֵן, meaning to praise them.

steps.title: This reading supports רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ברייתא backs up רב, who forbids saying "How beautiful is this גויה."
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רב, because רב said: A person may not say, "How beautiful is this gentile woman!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא's reading matches a ruling of רב. רב forbids praising the beauty of a גויה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב gave a ruling without naming a source. The ברייתא's reading of ״לֹא תְחׇנֵּם״ gives that ruling a source in the פסוק. Praising a גויה's beauty is one example of giving חֵן.

phrases.english: This supports רב,
as רב said:
It is forbidden for a person to say
"How beautiful is this gentile woman!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the ברייתא's reading to רב's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that one may not say "How beautiful is this גויה."
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's reading of ״לֹא תְחׇנֵּם״ as "do not give them חֵן."

steps.title: Two great רבנים reacted to a gentile woman's beauty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב with stories about רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי עקיבא, who both reacted openly to a gentile woman's beauty.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was standing on a step on הר הבית. He saw a very beautiful gentile woman and said, "How great are Your works, ה׳!" Also, רבי עקיבא saw the wife of the wicked טורנוסרופוס. He spat, laughed, and cried. He spat because she came from a putrid drop. He laughed because she would one day convert and he would marry her. He cried because all this beauty would one day rot in the dirt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with two stories. Both seem to go against רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל saw a beautiful גויה and said a פסוק that praises ה׳'s works, which sounds like praising her. רבי עקיבא also reacted to a גויה's beauty, so it seems allowed to notice it and talk about it.

keyTerms.meaning: A putrid drop (the seed a person starts from)

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: They challenged: There was a story with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה עַל גַּבֵּי מַעֲלָה בְּהַר הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: who was on a step on the Temple Mount,
and he saw one gentile woman who was extremely beautiful,
he said: "How great are Your works, ה׳!"
And רבי עקיבא too saw
the wife of the wicked טורנוסרופוס,
he spat, laughed, and cried.
He spat, because she came from a putrid drop;
phrases.notes: He means that every person, however beautiful, starts out from a drop of seed.

phrases.english: he laughed, because she was destined to convert and he would marry her;
he cried, because this beauty would rot in the dirt.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling that was just supported.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that one may not say "How beautiful is this גויה."
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל openly reacted to a גויה's beauty with words of praise, and רבי עקיבא also reacted to one. This suggests such praise is allowed.

steps.title: He was thanking ה׳, not praising her
steps.stepSummary: רב would say that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was thanking ה׳ for His creations, like the ברכה said when seeing beautiful creatures.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב? He would say: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was giving thanks to ה׳. As the Master said: One who sees beautiful creatures says, "Blessed is He who created such in His world."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was not praising the woman. He was thanking ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a difference between praising a person and praising ה׳ for what He made. חז״ל set a ברכה for seeing beautiful creatures, so thanking ה׳ at such a sight is clearly allowed. רב only forbids praising the גויה herself.

keyTerms.meaning: Who created such in His world (part of the ברכה)

steps.whatToRemember: Praising a גויה is forbidden by ״לֹא תְחׇנֵּם״. Thanking ה׳ for His beautiful creations is allowed, and even has its own ברכה.

phrases.english: And רב? He was giving thanks,
phrases.notes: Meaning: how would רב explain the story? He would say רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was thanking ה׳.

phrases.english: as the Master said:
One who sees beautiful creatures
says: "Blessed is He who created such in His world."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the story: the words were thanks to ה׳, not praise of the person.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל praised the beauty of the גויה, which goes against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was thanking ה׳, as in the ברכה for beautiful creatures. This does not break רב's rule.

steps.title: Was it even allowed to look at her?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether gazing at a woman is allowed at all, and begins a ברייתא that forbids gazing at women.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is it allowed to gaze at a woman? They challenged from a ברייתא: "And you shall guard yourself from every evil thing" means that a person should not gaze at a beautiful woman, even if she is unmarried, and not at a married woman, even if she is ugly,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new problem with the stories. Even if the words were thanks to ה׳, how could these רבנים look at the woman? The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא that forbids gazing at women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last answer fixed the problem of the words that were said. Now the challenge is the looking itself. The ברייתא learns from ״וְנִשְׁמַרְתָּ מִכֹּל דָּבָר רָע״ that gazing at a beautiful woman is forbidden even if she is single, and gazing at a married woman is forbidden even if she is not attractive. The ברייתא continues past this point.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge to רב's ruling about speaking. It is a new problem about the act of looking that the stories describe.

phrases.english: But is it permitted to gaze?
They challenged: "And you shall guard yourself from every evil thing"
means that a person should not gaze at a beautiful woman
even if she is unmarried,
and not at a married woman, even if she is ugly,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the words were explained as thanks to ה׳, the גמרא challenges the looking described in the stories.
steps.kashyaTarget: The stories in which רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי עקיבא looked at a beautiful גויה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא learns from ״וְנִשְׁמַרְתָּ מִכֹּל דָּבָר רָע״ that gazing at a beautiful woman is forbidden. So how could these רבנים look at her?
